session.name: MPI-449 two-stage H3 sampling proved; MpiNodes gained latent save/load, lazy gating and MpiH3Length

goal.original: Research MiniMax H3 on the bench before spending an engine bump on it; then build the MpiNodes save/load staging nodes for a two-stage H3 sample.
goal.summary: Two-stage sampling is SETTLED: splitting the sigma schedule 5/15 and round-tripping the latent through disk is bit-for-bit equal to a single-stage run, at +1.4 s (+4%) overhead. Four MpiNodes shipped and pushed. The blocker/OUTPUT_NODE laziness traps are fixed and documented, which opens the door to deleting the _stage2 workflow twins. The open risk: EVERY measurement on this card was taken at 56 frames, below H3 trained range of 124-362.

next_action.description: Re-run the step floor and timings at 124 frames (the shortest TRAINED length) using the h3_i2v bench workflow, which is already wired for it. Everything measured so far ran at 56 frames, under half the trained minimum, so the 5-step preview floor and the whole timing table are provisional. After that, bump node_lock.json to fd9bdca and test the lazy gating through the APP, not the browser.

key_decisions: Two-stage = split the SIGMA SCHEDULE (SplitSigmas step=5), not the model. Save SamplerCustomAdvanced.output (noisy); preview denoised_output (x0 estimate). Saving the denoised estimate and resuming from it is silently wrong.
Stage 2 must use DisableNoise and the low_sigmas tail of the SAME schedule. res_multistep resumes exactly; an ancestral/SDE sampler could not (its RNG state is not in the latent).
MpiH3Length snaps to the NEAREST valid frame count; core snaps UP, which is never closer.
MpiBlocker replaces MpiIfElseInverted on a preview tap - only MpiBlocker can be lazy.
The MpiNodes staging work was folded under MPI-449 rather than carded, at the user direction.
constraints: ExecutionBlocker travels DOWNSTREAM ONLY. A gate after a sampler has already paid for that sampler. Lazy inputs are the only mechanism that prevents upstream execution.
An OUTPUT_NODE is ALWAYS executed - ComfyUI seeds the run from every output node and walks back. This is why wan22_*_stage2.json exists (54 nodes vs 55, Stage1_Bypass deleted).

The browser prunes muted/bypassed nodes from the submitted prompt; the app submits every node and can only inject params. Same graph, different reachable set - this is why WAN passed in the browser and failed in the app.
H3 frame counts are n % 17 == 5 at 24 fps. Whole seconds are impossible below 8 s. Requested 2 s = 2.33 s = 56 frames, measured on a real mp4.
H3 trained range is 124-362 frames (5.17-15.08 s). ALL measurements on this card were at 56 frames.
H3 does NOT repeat frames (56 decoded, 56 unique) - the WAN/LTX remove-first-frame node is not needed.
comfy.nested_tensor is 0.30.0+; MpiNodes must import it INSIDE the function or the whole pack fails to load on the 0.29.2 app engine.
The bench runs with --output-directory D:/WORK/Images/Outputs - NOT G:/ComfyUi/ComfyUI/output. Cost two false negatives this session.
ComfyUI caches aggressively: a probe that deletes its output file still reads False if the node was cached. Vary an input to bust it; read execution_cached to learn what actually ran.
The bench is port 8188 (v0.30.2); the APP engine is 48188 (v0.29.2). Do not confuse them.
c:/AI/Mpi/ComfyUi-MpiNodes is NOT in permissions.additionalDirectories - writes there may prompt. Symlinked into the bench at custom_nodes/.

resume_prompt: You are resuming MPI-449, the umbrella card for bringing MiniMax H3 into Cubric Vision. Read .agents/mpi-kanban/tasks/MPI-449/research.md (sections 7-9 are this session) and docs/workflow-authoring/mpi-nodes.md before anything else. Two-stage H3 sampling is SETTLED and proved: splitting the sigma schedule 5/15 with a latent saved to disk between runs is bit-for-bit identical to a single-stage run, costing +1.4 s (+4%). Four nodes shipped to c:/AI/Mpi/ComfyUi-MpiNodes and pushed (HEAD fd9bdca): MpiSaveLatent, MpiLoadLatent, MpiBooleanInvert, MpiH3Length, plus a lazy-input fix to MpiBlocker. The big structural finding: ExecutionBlocker only travels downstream and an OUTPUT_NODE is always executed, so gating after a sampler never stopped the sampler - which is why the wan22_*_stage2.json twins exist. Both are now fixable with lazy gates, so those twins can likely be deleted. THE OPEN RISK: every measurement on this card - the 5-step preview floor, the pruned/unpruned A/B, the whole timing table - was taken at 56 frames, and H3 trained range is 124-362. Re-run at 124 before any of it becomes a tier default. Do not start the engine bump or the H3 model wiring; those are gated on MPI-451 (licence) and a 0.29.2 -> 0.30.x bump.
